title: Pods and the Workload Resources

header.html: Choose and use the right workload resource (Deployment, DaemonSet, CronJob, etc.)

toc.title: The Pod and the controllers that run it

html:
1The Pod and the controllers that run it

A Pod is the smallest unit you deploy: one or more containers that share a network address and volumes. You almost never run a bare Pod in real life, because nobody restarts it on another node if the node dies. You put a controller in front of it: the controller creates Pods from a template and keeps the right number running.

Object Use it for Pod names Key facts
Pod one-off tests, debugging the name you give no replacement if the node fails
Deployment stateless apps name-<hash>-<id> owns ReplicaSets; rolling updates and rollbacks (Module 5)
ReplicaSet keeps N Pods running name-<id> you rarely create it: a Deployment does
DaemonSet one Pod per node (agents, log shippers) name-<id> ignores replicas; needs tolerations for tainted nodes
StatefulSet apps that need a stable identity or storage name-0, name-1, ... governing Service (headless); ordered start
Job run to completion once name-<id> completions, parallelism, backoffLimit; restartPolicy is Never or OnFailure
CronJob Jobs on a schedule Job per run cron schedule; suspend pauses it

How to choose. Ask three questions. Does it run forever or finish? (forever: Deployment, DaemonSet, StatefulSet; finishes: Job, CronJob.) Does it need one copy per node? (DaemonSet.) Does each copy need its own name and disk? (StatefulSet; otherwise Deployment.)

2Create them fast

k run web --image=nginx:alpine --labels="app=web,tier=frontend" --env=MODE=prod --port=80
k create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=3
k create job once --image=busybox:1.36 -- sh -c "echo done"
k create cronjob tick --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="*/5 * * * *" -- date
k create job manual --from=cronjob/tick       # run a CronJob's template right now

A DaemonSet and a StatefulSet have no create command. Generate a Deployment with --dry-run=client -o yaml, change kind, delete replicas and strategy (a DaemonSet has neither), and add what is missing. A StatefulSet also needs serviceName and a headless Service.

# DaemonSet that also runs on the control plane node
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
        operator: Exists
        effect: NoSchedule
      containers: [...]

Imperative commands that change a controller: k scale deployment api --replicas=5, k set image deployment api nginx=nginx:stable-alpine, k set env deployment api MODE=prod, k label, k annotate, k patch, k edit.

3Jobs in detail

Field Meaning Default
completions how many Pods must finish successfully 1
parallelism how many Pods run at the same time 1
backoffLimit retries before the Job is marked failed 6
activeDeadlineSeconds total time limit for the whole Job none
ttlSecondsAfterFinished delete the finished Job (and its Pods) after this many seconds never
template.spec.restartPolicy must be Never or OnFailure (none: required)

restartPolicy: Always (the Pod default) is rejected in a Job: that is a classic "fix the manifest" task. With OnFailure the same Pod restarts its container; with Never a failed Pod stays and a new Pod is created (that is why backoffLimit counts Pods).

To wait for completion: k wait --for=condition=complete job/batch --timeout=120s. To read the output: k logs job/batch.

4CronJobs in detail

The schedule has five fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. */5 * * * * is every five minutes; 0 2 * * 1 is 02:00 every Monday. The schedule is evaluated in the controller's time zone unless you set timeZone.

Field Meaning
concurrencyPolicy Allow (default), Forbid (skip a run if the last one is still running), Replace (stop the old run and start the new one)
successfulJobsHistoryLimit / failedJobsHistoryLimit how many finished Jobs to keep (defaults 3 and 1)
startingDeadlineSeconds how late a missed run may still start
suspend true stops new runs without deleting the CronJob
jobTemplate the Job (with its Pod template) that each run creates

5StatefulSets in short

A StatefulSet gives each Pod a stable name (db-0, db-1), starts them in order, and with volumeClaimTemplates gives each its own PersistentVolumeClaim (Module 4). A headless Service (clusterIP: None) gives each Pod its own DNS name: db-0.db.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local. Set serviceName to that Service. Deleting a StatefulSet does not delete its PVCs.

6Self-healing basics

  • A Pod's restartPolicy (Always, OnFailure, Never) tells the kubelet when to restart a failed container. Controllers set what they need; a bare Pod defaults to Always.
  • A Deployment replaces Pods that disappear; a Job replaces Pods that fail (up to backoffLimit); a DaemonSet replaces a missing node Pod.
  • Delete a Pod owned by a controller and a new one appears: to stop it, delete the controller.
Exam tip

. Read the kind in the task. "Run on every node" is a DaemonSet, "run once and finish" is a Job, "run every night" is a CronJob. The wrong kind scores zero even if the container runs.

Exam tip

. k create job --from=cronjob/<name> <job> starts a CronJob's work now; tasks ask for it.

7Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m02 -->

Lab 2.1: pod spec

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m02-01-pod-spec)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace wl, create a Pod named web with the image nginx:alpine, the labels app=web and tier=frontend, the environment variable MODE=prod, and the container port 80 declared. Wait until it is Running.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n wl run web --image=nginx:alpine --labels="app=web,tier=frontend" --env=MODE=prod --port=80
kubectl -n wl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/web --timeout=120s

Lab 2.2: deployment template label

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m02-02-deployment-template-label)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace wl, create a Deployment named api with the image nginx:alpine and 3 replicas. Then add the label tier=backend to the Pods that the Deployment creates (that is, to the Pod template), so that kubectl get pods -l tier=backend lists 3 Ready Pods. Wait for the rollout to finish.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n wl create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=3
kubectl -n wl patch deployment api -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"tier":"backend"}}}}}'
kubectl -n wl rollout status deployment api --timeout=120s
kubectl -n wl get pods -l tier=backend

Lab 2.3: job completions

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m02-03-job-completions)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace wl, create a Job named batch with the image busybox:1.36 that runs sh -c "echo done". It must run 4 Pods to completion in total, 2 at a time (completions: 4, parallelism: 2), and be retried at most 2 times on failure (backoffLimit: 2). Wait until the Job is complete.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n wl create job batch --image=busybox:1.36 --dry-run=client -o yaml -- sh -c "echo done" > /tmp/batch.yaml
sed -i 's/^spec:/spec:\n  completions: 4\n  parallelism: 2\n  backoffLimit: 2/' /tmp/batch.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/batch.yaml
kubectl -n wl wait --for=condition=complete job/batch --timeout=180s

Lab 2.4: cronjob settings

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m02-04-cronjob-settings)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace wl, create a CronJob named tick with the image busybox:1.36 that runs date every 5 minutes. It must not start a run while the previous one is still running (concurrencyPolicy: Forbid), and keep the last 2 successful and the last 1 failed Jobs. Then start one run now, by creating a Job named tick-manual from the CronJob, and wait until that Job is complete.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n wl create cronjob tick --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="*/5 * * * *" -- date
kubectl -n wl patch cronjob tick -p '{"spec":{"concurrencyPolicy":"Forbid","successfulJobsHistoryLimit":2,"failedJobsHistoryLimit":1}}'
kubectl -n wl create job tick-manual --from=cronjob/tick
kubectl -n wl wait --for=condition=complete job/tick-manual --timeout=180s

Lab 2.5: daemonset all nodes

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m02-05-daemonset-all-nodes)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace wl, create a DaemonSet named agent with the image busybox:1.36 that runs sleep 3600. It must run one Pod on every node of the cluster, including the control plane node (which has a NoSchedule taint). Wait until all its Pods are Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n wl create deployment agent --image=busybox:1.36 --dry-run=client -o yaml -- sleep 3600 > /tmp/ds.yaml
sed -i 's/kind: Deployment/kind: DaemonSet/; /replicas: 1/d; /strategy: {}/d' /tmp/ds.yaml
sed -i 's/^      containers:/      tolerations:\n      - key: node-role.kubernetes.io\/control-plane\n        operator: Exists\n        effect: NoSchedule\n      containers:/' /tmp/ds.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/ds.yaml
kubectl -n wl rollout status daemonset agent --timeout=120s
kubectl -n wl get pods -o wide

Lab 2.6: fix job manifest

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m02-06-fix-job-manifest)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The file ~/work/report-job.yaml defines the Job report in the namespace wl, but kubectl apply -f rejects it. Fix the file without changing the Job name, the image or the command, create the Job, and wait until it is complete.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f ~/work/report-job.yaml
sed -i 's/restartPolicy: Always/restartPolicy: Never/' ~/work/report-job.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/work/report-job.yaml
kubectl -n wl wait --for=condition=complete job/report --timeout=120s

Lab 2.7: statefulset headless

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m02-07-statefulset-headless)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace wl, create a headless Service named db (port 80, selecting Pods with the label app=db) and a StatefulSet named db with 2 replicas of the image nginx:alpine, whose serviceName is db and whose Pods carry the label app=db. Wait until the Pods db-0 and db-1 are Ready. The name db-0.db.wl.svc.cluster.local must answer on port 80 from inside the cluster.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n wl apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: db}
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector: {app: db}
  ports: [{port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: db}
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: db}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: db}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:alpine
Y
kubectl -n wl rollout status statefulset db --timeout=180s

<!-- /LABS -->

8Recall questions

R1Which workload resource runs one Pod on every node?

Show the answer

A DaemonSet.

R2Which restartPolicy values are allowed in a Job's Pod template?

Show the answer

Never or OnFailure.

R3What do completions and parallelism mean in a Job?

Show the answer

Completions is how many Pods must succeed in total; parallelism is how many run at the same time.

R4What does concurrencyPolicy: Forbid do on a CronJob?

Show the answer

It skips a new run while the previous run is still running.

R5Which command starts a CronJob's work immediately?

Show the answer

kubectl create job <name> --from=cronjob/<cronjob>.

R6What does a StatefulSet's serviceName point to?

Show the answer

A headless Service (clusterIP: None) that gives the Pods stable DNS names.

R7How do you make a DaemonSet Pod run on the tainted control plane node?

Show the answer

Add a toleration for the node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane NoSchedule taint.

R8Why use a Deployment instead of a bare Pod?

Show the answer

The controller replaces Pods that fail or disappear and provides rolling updates; a bare Pod is not replaced.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Choose forever: Deployment; per node: DaemonSet; stable identity: StatefulSet; once: Job; schedule: CronJob
Fast create run, create deployment, create job, create cronjob; --from=cronjob/x
No create command DaemonSet, StatefulSet: generate a Deployment YAML and edit
Job completions, parallelism, backoffLimit, restartPolicy Never/OnFailure
CronJob five-field schedule, concurrencyPolicy, history limits, suspend
StatefulSet name-0, headless Service, serviceName
DaemonSet no replicas; tolerate the control plane taint to reach all nodes
